BiblicalUsage: David says, 'I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears' — and Isaiah promises a day when the ransomed of the LORD shall return to Zion with songs, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away. The word is the noun for the sigh itself: David's night of tears on one side, and the day sighing ends on the other.
TheologicalSignificance: Sighing is the sound of sorrow, and Isaiah's promise is that it will flee away: the ransomed come home singing, and I believe that is where every sigh is headed.
